title: A client connection as the Redis 8 server holds it (CLIENT LIST)

sources.ref: redis 8.10.2 src/anet.c:113-252 anetKeepAlive(): on Linux idle = tcp-keepalive, intvl = idle/3 (min 1), cnt = 3
Redis CLIENT LIST documentation (id, addr, laddr, fd, name, age, idle, flags, cmd ...)

redis 8.10.2 (and 7.4.1) src/timeout.c:146-180 getTimeoutFromObjectOrReply(): the deadline is commandTimeSnapshot() plus ceil(timeout × 1000) ms; src/timeout.c:118-136 handleBlockedClientsTimeout(): a deadline fires once mstime() is past it, from blockedBeforeSleep() (src/blocked.c:827); src/ae.c:383-404 aeProcessEvents(): beforeSleep, then a sleep until the earliest time event; src/server.c:1859 serverCron returns 1000/hz ms; src/server.c:1572-1584 dynamic-hz doubles hz only while clients exceed 200 a tick

redis 8.10.2 (and 7.4.1) src/timeout.c clientsCronHandleTimeout(): closes when now/1000 − lastinteraction > maxidletime, in whole seconds, and never for a blocked or Pub/Sub client; src/server.c:1259-1271 clientsCron visits every client each serverCron when it holds fewer than 5

CONNECTED.note: listed by CLIENT LIST; flags and cmd change within it

BLOCKED.note: blocked on a command with a timeout (BLPOP and the other blocking commands): its reply waits for data on a key, or for the timeout

GONE.note: freed; the id is never reused within a server process

peer.fin.note: read returns 0: the client closed (QUIT included)

peer.data.note: a segment from the client (re-arms the keepalive idle timer)

app.quit.note: QUIT: the server replies and closes (close after reply)

socket.error.note: read fails with the socket's own error: the kernel beneath gave up, by its keepalive or its retransmissions (ETIMEDOUT)

app.block.note: a blocking command with a timeout above 0, which puts the client in the timeout table

app.unblock.note: data on a key it waits for serves it, and its reply goes out

timer.blocked.note: the blocking command's timeout: its null reply goes out

hz.note: the kernel's build option: Redis's keepalive is the kernel's, so its firings are rounded on the kernel's timer wheel, which counts in jiffies

blocking_timeout.note: the blocking command's own timeout argument, in seconds (0 blocks for ever): a cell gives it

redis_hz.note: how often serverCron runs; an idle event loop sleeps until it

idle.note: the timeout config (0 = off): clientsCron closes a client once the whole seconds since its last interaction exceed it, so never early and up to 1 s and one serverCron tick late. Each command it reads re-arms it. A blocked or Pub/Sub client has none

blocked.note: the deadline is the command's start, in whole ms, plus the timeout rounded up to the ms, and beforeSleep fires it only once the clock is past it, so never early. An idle event loop calls beforeSleep only when it wakes, at the next serverCron, so the reply goes up to one tick and 1 ms late (101 ms at hz 10). Traffic on any other socket wakes it sooner

systems.mechanism.idle-refresh-interval.note: the keepalive timer's first firing, when the first probe refreshes an idle flow: its idle time, rounded up on the wheel

client-list.note: polled; appearance and disappearance are bracketed by two polls

over.note: Redis holds each client on a Linux TCP socket, and anetKeepAlive sets its keepalive from tcp-keepalive alone: the idle time, a third of it in whole seconds and at least 1, and 3 probes. So its detection of a dead client is the kernel's keepalive, or its retransmissions when a reply is unacknowledged, and either reaches Redis as a read error.
